cards.verifier_reason: A: the card's own price series fails the test it passes it on. FY2023 price effect +4.8% against US CPI +4.1% (Legrand FY2023 release, 14 Feb 2024) sits inside a three-year window at a 3 Sep 2026 scoring date, and the only cited pass point is one half-year (+2.9%, H1 2026) with no FY2024 or FY2025 price effect cited; price is a fail on the series, or silent for want of a cited series, and either route charges -1 (one fail, or fewer than two testable), so A 15 to 14. C1: the move to 5 rests on 'no ceiling exists under the v2.1 table', which is wrong. The table lists kWh delivered for energy_access and ghg, and the card itself cites the figure (IEA Energy and AI, Apr 2025: about 415 TWh data-centre electricity 2024, about 200 TWh 2020); the unbounded-consumption rule is scoped to person-counts, not to an energy-agency kWh count. Only penetration is missing, which closes the 6-7 bounded sub-clause but not the neutral band: enlarging is recorded as none and demand tracks construction, renovation and data-centre capex, drivers Legrand does not create. C1 returns to 6, and the WSIOF card in this same batch keeps C1 at 7 with penetration also not computable, so the two cards cannot both be right. Total 64 unchanged in sum, wrong in composition; the stated basis of the tier move is refuted. C2 6 is carried against a recorded induced rebound (IEA series) and is the top of neutral; noted, not corrected.
